jobs.occupation: Hands-on Data Engineer or Architect | Databricks & AWS, Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about turning data into meaningful business impact? Do you enjoy collaborating with others to solve complex challenges and building modern data platforms that enable better decisions?

At Valcon, we’re growing our Data & AI community and are looking for a Data Engineer who combines technical curiosity with a collaborative mindset. We are particularly interested in professionals with strong Databricks and AWS experience who want to help shape innovative data solutions for some of Denmark’s leading organisations.

The role

As an experienced Data Engineer at Valcon, you’ll work closely with clients, architects, data scientists, and fellow engineers to design, build, and use scalable cloud-based data platforms. You will play a key role in helping organisations transform data into insights, AI solutions, and business value. A significant part of the role will involve working with Databricks and AWS, designing modern data platforms, building robust data pipelines, implementing modern AI/BI tooling, and supporting clients throughout their transformation journeys. Depending on the project, you’ll also work with technologies such as Azure, Python, SQL, Terraform, and PySpark.

What you bring along

• Minimum of 5 years of experience building and using modern data platforms based on Databricks and AWS

• Preferably fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken

• Strong data engineering skills, including data integration, ETL/ELT pipelines, and data modelling

• Familiar with engineering best practices, CI/CD, DevOps, testing, and automation

• Experience from regulated industries such as Life Sciences, Financial Services, Tax Administration, or Defence is an advantage

• A collaborative mindset with a passion for solving complex challenges and creating impact together with clients and colleagues

Why join Valcon?

At Valcon, you’ll become part of a collaborative and welcoming community where knowledge sharing, continuous learning, and professional development are a natural part of everyday life. We offer exciting projects, a transparent career framework, certification opportunities, and strong support for your professional growth. We also believe that great work happens when people thrive, which is why we place a strong emphasis on flexibility, well-being, and family-friendly benefits. Beyond our client work, our community comes together through both professional and social activities, creating an environment where people can build meaningful relationships and feel a sense of belonging.

Interested?

We are looking for talented professionals who are excited by this opportunity and can contribute to our team. While you may not meet every requirement, you should bring strong relevant experience and a genuine passion for data and technology. We invite candidates ongoing to interviews.

jobs.occupation: Internship in Water Ecosystem and Business Development
jobs.description:
Would you like to be part of Kamstrup Water’s business development journey, and do you have a passion for solutions that drive sustainable growth? Are you ready to get hands-on experience with Business Development while working on the digital footprint within our Water division? Do you want to kick-start your career and turn your theoretical knowledge into practical experience in an international company?

Here is what the job entails

As an intern in our Water Ecosystem and Business Development team, you will collaborate closely with experienced colleagues to shape the next generation of solutions for water utilities. Your work will focus on exploring the right technologies, markets, and potential partners during the innovation phase. This includes identifying impactful solutions, creating pilots, and generating value propositions and business cases to guide future priorities.

More specifically you will be:

• Conducting desk research to investigate competitive solutions, markets, and potential partners.

• Participating in workshops and webinars to gain insights and foster collaboration.

• Contributing to idea generation sessions with customers or stakeholders to drive innovation.

• Supporting the development of business cases for promising opportunities.

• Assisting in managing projects related to the development and implementation of new solutions.

Meet your future team

You will become a part of a department, that focuses on Business Development within Kamstrup Water business unit. The team consists of 2 dedicated employees and a student worker and is characterized by a youthful atmosphere where new ideas and sparring are the backbone of everything we do. The department is responsible for the expansion and growth of future solutions in the water solutions portfolio on a global scale.

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for an analytical-minded student who strives to create valuable commercial impact on our Water business unit. You have a commercial focus combined with a solution orientation mindset which empowers you to translate customer challenges into solutions.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Are studying Global Business Engineering, Business & Water Technology, or a relevant MSc in Economics and Business Administration, Business Development, Business Management, Digital Business Management, or similar. That being said, there are many entry points to this position

• As a person have a curious and creative mindset, allowing you to proactively seek new knowledge and thereby provide new ideas and challenge status quo

• Have a structured approach to your work, enabling you to manage several ongoing tasks while maintaining an overview

• Naturally strive towards ensuring quality results whether you are collaborating with colleagues or working independently

As we are an international organisation it is important that you are fluent in English.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, this is an internship position, and we value curiosity and a willingness to learn just as much as experience. If the role interests you and you are motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply.

We offer more than just an internship

At Kamstrup, your contribution as an intern is highly valued, and we cherish the good colleagueship. Therefore, you will experience an internship with a strong focus on your individual development through challenging tasks, career sparring, voluntary courses, as well as social events and a large network. We are proud, that our internship program has resulted in Studenterhus Aarhus granting us with the Mentor Award, the Internationalization Award, the Jury’s Special Award and the award for East Jutland’s Best Internship.

Besides the best program, we also offer:

• A gratuity which may be provided in recognition of your efforts if your place of study allows it as well as paid public transportation to and from work

• Multiple internship events and weekly internship lunches

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association, that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

The applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, but you can expect a response within six weeks. Any details about the internship will be individually agreed upon. However, the internship is expected to run from the beginning of February 2027 until the end of June 2027.

Kamstrup is located in Stilling south of Aarhus, and bus number 200 takes you right to the door.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Business Development Manager, Amalie Lund, on telephone nr.: +45 89 93 10 00.

Are you curious about how digital regulation and regulatory compliance come to life in an international technology company? Would you like to contribute to meaningful legal work within areas such as data protection, AI, cybersecurity and technology law while learning from experienced professionals along the way? Are you ready to kick-start your career with a student job that combines digital regulation with real responsibility?

Here is what the job entails

In this role, you will gain practical experience with digital regulation and regulatory compliance through hands-on legal tasks while supporting our Regulatory Compliance team. You will contribute to a wide range of legal and compliance activities that help ensure the organisation meets its regulatory obligations and supports responsible business practices.

More specifically, you will be:

• Conducting legal research and information searches within data protection and other areas of digital regulation

• Contributing to practical compliance activities, including preparing and maintaining legally required data protection documentation

• Assisting in drafting, reviewing and updating data processing agreements and other compliance-related documentation

• Supporting the ongoing oversight of data processors and sub-processors to help ensure compliance with applicable data protection requirements

• Contributing to other legal and regulatory matters based on the team’s priorities and ongoing projects.

In this role, you will join an engaged and collaborative team that supports your development while giving you plenty of opportunities to learn and take on meaningful responsibility. You will also gain valuable insight into how regulatory compliance informs business decisions and supports strategic initiatives across an international technology company.

Meet your future team

You will become part of our Regulatory Compliance team within the Commercial & Legal Services Department. Together, we help Kamstrup navigate legal and regulatory requirements while supporting the company’s strategic goals and international activities. Our team is characterised by close collaboration, open communication and mutual support. Knowledge sharing and professional discussions are a natural part of our everyday work, and we value curiosity, positivity, engagement and different perspectives.

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for a motivated and curious student who is eager to apply legal knowledge in practice while bringing your own perspectives and ideas to the team. You have a desire to learn while also being curious about how legal and regulatory requirements shape business decisions. Most importantly, you bring a positive attitude, a genuine desire to contribute to the team's success, and a strong engagement, allowing you to go the extra mile during peak periods.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Are currently studying law or business law and have completed at least the 5th semester of the degree

• Have a strong interest in developing your knowledge of data protection, regulatory compliance and digital legislation

• Are comfortable conducting legal research and analysing complex information

• Pay attention to details and are committed to delivering high-quality work

• Communicate effectively and can collaborate and build strong relationships across different functions

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English and Danish.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

We are more than an ordinary workplace

We offer a challenging student job in an international company where you are given independent responsibility for specific assignments, and where you can transform your theoretical knowledge into practical experience. As a student worker, you will be treated as an integrated part of the team, equal to other employees, ensuring a steep learning curve.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work-life balance through flexible working hours

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

Please submit your application by using the link below. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and you can expect a response within six weeks.This is a part-time position of approximately 15 hours per week. Your working hours will be agreed individually, with flexibility during examination periods.

The job will be located at Kamstrup's headquarters in Stilling, between Aarhus and Skanderborg.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Legal Counsel, Camilla Hovgaard Svare, on phone: +45 89 93 10 00.

Context & Environment

Join TotalEnergies EP Danmark, a key player in energy production in the North Sea.

Within the Logistics & Support to Operations (LSO) team based in Esbjerg and reporting to the Head of Methods, you will contribute to improving the subsidiary’s logistics performance through data analysis, process optimization, development of digital tools, and implementation of continuous improvement projects supporting offshore operations.

Please check your eligibility for the VIE program and the country-specific requirements on the following website: https://mon-vie-via.businessfrance.fr/qu-est-ce-que-le-volontariat-international

Activities

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Develop and maintain management dashboards.

• Participate in reporting automation and data quality improvement.

• Conduct cost and operational efficiency analyses.

• Map and optimize supply chain processes.

• Participate in the improvement of digital tools and SAP solutions.

• Contribute to the development of digitalization projects under SharePoint.

• Support the deployment of new logistics and analytical tools.

Why join us ?

A minimum C1 level of English is required. A minimum B2 level of French is also required.

Additional Information

jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions
jobs.description:
Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions  Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
 University of Copenhagen

  The University seeks to appoint a tenure track assistant professor to commence 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  Information on the department can be found at: http://www.sund.ku.dk/. 

  Subject area: Infectious disease epidemiology, modelling, animal health, One Health, and sustainable health systems

  The Tenure-Track Assistant Professor will lead research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, with particular emphasis on how changes in environmental conditions, animal populations, production systems, and management practices influence disease emergence, transmission, and control. The position will combine infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical and statistical modelling, data science, and economic analysis to generate evidence supporting disease preparedness, prevention, and control.

  The successful candidate will:

   	
• Lead independent research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, including the influence of environmental and production system changes. 	
• Develop and apply simulation, epidemiological, and statistical models to assess disease and spillover risks, evaluate mitigation and control strategies, and quantify their economic implications. 	
• Demonstrate strong programming skills in R and other relevant programming languages, including experience in managing, processing, and analysing large and complex datasets. 	
• Have experience in developing and applying epidemiological disease-spread models, including model calibration, validation, parameter estimation, and calculation of epidemiological indicators such as the basic reproduction number (R₀) across different animal species and production systems. 	
• Design and implement epidemiological modelling frameworks. 	
• Validate and calibrate models using large-scale national datasets, ensuring scientific robustness, methodological validity, and relevance for policy and decision-making. 	
• Translate research findings into evidence supporting risk-based disease prevention, preparedness, and control.  	
• Establish and maintain collaborations with key stakeholders, including the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, industry partners such as SEGES and Landbrug & Fødevarer (L&F), and international organisations such as the FAO. 	
• Lead and secure independent research funding through competitive national and international funding calls. The position requires demonstrated experience in securing external funding, as well as the ambition to develop research ideas into externally funded projects and provide scientific leadership for such projects within the TIPTON Research Group. 	
• Contribute to the development and delivery of One Health and sustainability teaching, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, disease preparedness, and the interactions between animal, human, and environmental health. 	
• Contribute to teaching in data science, including data management, dataset preparation and handling, statistical analysis, programming, and the analysis of large-scale and complex datasets. 	
• Supervise students and contribute to research capacity building within infectious disease epidemiology, disease modelling, data science, and One Health. 	
• Contribute to the delivery of government services undertaken by the Department, including research-based advice, preparedness activities, risk assessments, and other activities relevant to infectious disease modelling and control.   The position is expected to combine methodological excellence in infectious disease modelling and data science with applied epidemiological research, generating evidence that is directly relevant to disease preparedness, private and public bodies, sustainable production systems, animal health and resilient health systems.

  The tenure track assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• research, including publication/academic dissemination 	
• research-based teaching  	
• sharing knowledge with society  	
• participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors    The tenure track assistant professor’s performance will be evaluated through annual evaluations. Furthermore, the tenure track assistant professor will be evaluated in a mid-track appraisal. 

  After no more than six years of employment and on condition of a positive final appraisal, the tenure track assistant professor will be employed as associate professor. Find more information about tenure track at the University of Copenhagen.

  Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for an assistant professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• a PhD degree or similar qualifications within the subject area  	
• research experience within the field of the position    The tenure track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact. 

  The assistant professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills. 

  Salary and employment conditions
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is permanent. 

  Employment is as Tenure Track Assistant Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. 

  There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector at www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

  Questions 
 For further information, please contact Research Group Leader: Professor Beate Conrady, bcon@sund.ku.dk

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application 
 The application must be submitted in English, and must include the following documents: 

   	
• Application (Including motivation for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD and other relevant diplomas) 	
• A complete list of publications  	
• Research plan (2-4 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 publications to be considered in the assessment  	
• Teaching portfolio, if applicable (Guidelines)   Please note: It is mandatory to upload a teaching plan in the online application form. Should you not be able to produce a teaching plan, please upload a blank document in this box instead.

  Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation. 

  The application will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested in this post to apply. 

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, 18 November 2026.

  Interviews for this position are likely to be held on 7 April 2027.

Job Description

Depending on the project and customer, you may become part of either our Application Services or Consulting business area. • Automation of business processes through, for example, batch jobs.

• Development of tools and scripts for data migration and other technical solutions.

• Are newly graduated or have a couple of years of experience. Most importantly, you are passionate about taking your IT career to the next level.

• Have fundamental knowledge of software development and are motivated to develop your competencies.

• Think analytically, show initiative, and work in a structured way.

Continue developing with us

The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Send us your application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

At MFT Energy, we innovate energy trading through our people and technology.

Are you curious about how risk is managed in one of the fastest-moving industries in the world? At MFT Energy, we are looking for a Student Risk Analyst who wants to gain hands-on experience working with data and risk management in a dynamic energy trading environment.

The role as a Student Risk Analyst:

You will join our Finance, Risk & Treasury department, where you will be part of our Risk team working alongside experienced colleagues with deep industry expertise. The team works closely with stakeholders across the trading organization to provide transparency on the company’s overall risk profile and support informed decision-making.

In a business characterized by rapidly changing market conditions and significant volatility, the Risk team helps ensure a responsible balance between risk and return across all our trading activities.

In this role, you will work with a wide range of datasets, including trade data and market price data that form the foundation of our risk calculations. Through this work, you will contribute to maintaining reliable risk data and develop a strong understanding of how risk management supports a modern energy trading company.

The position offers a steep learning curve in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same.

Your key responsibilities:

• Working with large trade and market price datasets to ensure the quality of risk calculations

• Developing data quality checks within our in-house data models

• Improving existing tools and developing new solutions (primarily using SQL, Power BI, Power Automate, and Power Apps)

• Automating tasks related to reporting, data processing and analysis

• Supporting the risk business partners with daily ad hoc tasks and analysis

• Gaining exposure to different types of risks including liquidity, market, credit and operational risk

Your qualifications and personal skills:

• Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Economics, Finance, Mathematics or a similar field.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

• Ability to work independently and take initiative

• Coding skills are a plus but not required. The most important thing is an interest in learning, as much of the data work will involve SQL

• Interest in energy markets and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment

• Curious and open-minded approach to learning and problem-solving

Working in MFT Energy

At MFT Energy, we combine a startup mindset with the strength of a global organization. We believe in empowering individuals to make data-driven decisions in a fast-paced environment. We are around 200 employees working out of our headquarters in Scandinavian Center, Aarhus C, and from our international offices in Turkey, Australia, New York, Singapore, Japan, and several remote colleagues working from all over the world.

We offer:

• A 15–20-hour student position with flexibility to plan your working hours around your studies

• A role where you will take ownership of your tasks while working closely with experienced colleagues who are always ready to support and spar with you

• An international and fast-moving environment where things develop quickly and you will continuously learn new things

• A strong student community and plenty of social activities, such as CrossFit, running club, Friday bars, team events, and more

jobs.occupation: A Post doc position is available in the Grønbæk Group at Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC),
jobs.description:
We are searching for a skilled and experienced post doc with specific interest in investigating early myeloid disease, clonal haematopoiesis, metabolism and obesity.

  Our research/The group

  The focus of the Grønbæk group is Translational Haematology. The group is affiliated with Biotech Research and Innovation centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen and Rigshospitalet (Central Copenhagen University Hospital). 

  Our overall aim is to understand the molecular mechanisms of haematological cancers and based on this; to design, develop and implement novel, scientifically based, clinical trials, with a strong focus on epigenetic therapies. This is done by bridging between clinical research at Rigshospitalet and the basic cancer biology research at BRIC, and in international collaborations with, among others, the Van Andel Research Institute, Michigan, USA and the Nordic MDS study group.

  Our location at the Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC provides optimal conditions for interaction with the basic scientists at BRIC. The group currently consists of 14 scientists, MD/scientists and students, one clinical research coordinator, 1 research nurse and 2 biomedical laboratory scientists.

   

  The project: Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms.

  The current position is part of a joint project ‘Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms’ together with Professor George Vassiliou, Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom funded by a ‘Molecular Mechanisms Linking Obesity and Cancer (MMLOC)’ grant from the Novo Nordisk foundation, which supports collaborative research projects with the purpose ‘to reverse-translate clinical observations into mechanistic studies that will increase our understanding of how obesity impacts carcinogenesis’.

  Obesity is a global health issue linked to increased risk of cancer, including blood cancers such as myeloid neoplasms (MN). Many MN arise from clonal haematopoiesis (CH)—the abnormal expansion of blood stem cell clones carrying somatic mutations. Haematopoietic stem cells interact with bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT), which increases with obesity, which may fuel CH growth and progression to MN. Epidemiological and genetic studies already suggest obesity accelerates CH, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

  This project integrates large-scale population data, clinical trials, and mechanistic mouse studies to investigate these links and explore preventive or therapeutic strategies.

   

  Your job

  The project focuses on translational analyses of live frozen human cells from patient bone marrow (BM)/(BMAT) and blood samples from completed and ongoing clinical trials. We are searching for a skilled post doc who is very interactive and enjoys collaborations with other scientists – including younger scientists and clinician scientists.

  Your tasks will include:

   	
• Process of live frozen patient material from clinical trials including isolation of defined cell populations, and quality control for downstream omics 	
• Perform in-house molecular techniques which may include Proteomics, PCR, ddPCR, and library/sample preparation for RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and DNA methylation analyses 	
• Coordinate genomic, transcriptomic, lipidomic, metabolomic analyses with our internal and external collaborating laboratories and take the lead on designing relevant sub-studies, integrating and interpreting the data 	
• Help establish the practical and regulatory framework for these collaborations, including material transfer and data-sharing agreements 	
• Participate in grant and manuscript writing 	
• Present at local and international meetings 	
• Introduce lab techniques to new lab members and students 	
• Collaborate with both scientists and clinicians   Start: February 1st, 2027

  Duration: 2 years

  Profile

  We expect you to be a highly motivated and highly ambitious, independent scientist with the following qualifications: •

   	
• A PhD in Life Sciences with a preferred focus on haematology 	
• A strong background in mechanisms of normal and malignant haematopoiesis and molecular haematology techniques 	
• Comprehensive lab skills in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including work with primary human cells and cryopreserved patient material 	
• Experience with genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, lipidomics, metabolomics and ability to analyse and interpret such data 	
• Experience with running projects across research groups 	
• Strong publication and presentation record in peer reviewed journals and international conferences 	
• Excellent written and spoken English skills 	
• Very collaborative 	
• Good social skills     

  Place of employment
 The workplace is at the Bartholin Institute which is part of Rigshospitalet, University of Copenhagen. The Bartholin Institute is located at Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC, close to the centre of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and a number of core facilities (animal unit, flow cytometry, in vivo imaging, NGS, etc.) shared between the research groups at BRIC (www.bric.ku.dk) and the neighbouring Finsen Laboratory. We have weekly journal clubs, data clubs, seminars with invited speakers and a young researchers club ASAP and our own PhD programme, MoMeD.

   

  Terms of employment 
 The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of two years. The starting date is 01.02.2027 or after agreement.
 Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,900 DKK/approx. 5,300 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025

   

  Questions 

  For further information regarding the position, please contact Professor Kirsten Grønbæk, kirsten groenbaek@regionh.dk; phone + 4535456086 / +4525211598.

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

   

  Application
 The application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page).

  2. CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position.

  3. A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do.

  4. List of publications.

   

  Recommendation 
 Furthermore, the applicant should provide two letters of recommendation or two references. To be taken into consideration, the letters must be signed by the supporting person on paper with institutional letter head and in PDF-format.

   

  Application deadline 15 November 2026, 23.59pm CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications 3 of 4 or letters of recommendation that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

   

  The further process

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.
